subject: biology

items.correct: As electrical signals along neurones, passed chemically across synapses.
items.misconception: As electricity flowing through wires inside the body.
items.random_wrong: As hormones carried in the blood.
items.why: Impulses are electrical along a neurone but cross the gap between neurones (synapse) using chemical transmitters.

items.q: How do hormonal responses compare with nervous responses?
items.correct: Hormonal responses are usually slower and longer-lasting.
items.misconception: Hormones act instantly, exactly like nerves.
items.random_wrong: Hormones only work while you are asleep.
items.why: Nervous responses are fast and short-lived; hormonal responses are slower but last longer.

items.correct: No — they are rapid and automatic, often via the spinal cord.
items.misconception: Yes, you choose to carry out each reflex.
items.random_wrong: Reflexes only happen in the brain after thinking.
items.why: Reflexes bypass conscious thought for speed, protecting the body (e.g. pulling away from a pin).

items.q: Do sensory and motor neurones do the same job?
items.correct: No — sensory carry impulses to the CNS, motor carry them away to effectors.
items.misconception: Yes, the same neurone carries impulses both ways.
items.random_wrong: Only motor neurones exist in humans.
items.why: The pathway is receptor → sensory neurone → CNS → motor neurone → effector.

specSource: CCEA GCSE Biology (2017) specification; Coordination & Control
